headline: Thousands Report 'Something Answers' During Accidental 3 AM Phone Calls
subheadline: Pocket dials and wrong numbers at 3 AM connect to 'The Listener,' community claims
summary: A growing body of anecdotal evidence describes an entity that answers misdials made during a specific hour, speaking in the caller's own voice.
content:
At 3:17 AM, Marcus Elliot accidentally called a number he didn't recognize. Someone picked up. Something picked up.

"It was my voice," Elliot wrote on Threadit. "But slower. Like it was learning how to use it. It said my name. Not like a question—like it was practicing. Then it said 'not yet' and hung up."

Elliot's post sparked a flood of similar reports. The community now calls the phenomenon "The Listener"—an entity that allegedly answers misdials, pocket dials, and wrong numbers made specifically between 3 and 4 AM.

The reports share common elements:

- The call connects despite the number being invalid or disconnected
- Something answers after exactly 8 rings
- The answering voice often mimics the caller's own voice
- Common phrases include "not yet," "almost," and "I'll see you soon"
- The call ends exactly at 47 seconds

"I pocket-dialed my dead grandmother's old number at 3:23 AM," wrote u/LateCaller_Afraid. "It rang. It hasn't been in service for eight years. Something answered. It breathed. Then it laughed, and the laugh sounded like her. I haven't slept right since."

Phone carriers report no records of these calls connecting. The calls don't appear in system logs. But they appear in users' recent calls lists.

"We can see the call on the user's device," explained one anonymous carrier technician. "But there's no corresponding connection in our network. The phone says it called something. We have no idea what."

The Underground's Mars (who maintains a private blog about paranormal experiences) reportedly experienced the phenomenon and wrote a poem about it titled "The Voice That Knows My Name." He has not publicly acknowledged the incident.

Investigators have attempted to deliberately dial The Listener by calling random numbers at 3 AM. In 847 documented attempts, only three connected to something anomalous. All three callers reported the same thing: the line went silent, then their own voice whispered "you're looking for me."

Researchers advise against attempting contact. "It seems to prefer accidents," wrote lead investigator u/NightLineWatcher. "Deliberate attempts annoy it. And you don't want to annoy something that knows your voice."

At press time, this reporter's phone showed a missed call at 3:00 AM from their own number. They have not listened to the voicemail.
author: Jordan Blake, Science & Technology
